{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6NMcfG5bLSSJ6TwvbS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019ABKECSVuk3SEJ8uzrQsPK","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-004/2026-07-24T150845Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Mobile WalletConnect deep-linking on Stake\n\n## 1. Why nothing auto-opened before the patch\n\nOn mobile the dApp runs in a browser tab and Rainbow is a **separate app**. There is no shared process, no injected `window.ethereum`. The WalletConnect v2 connection is a session over the WC **relay** (a websocket to a relay server). When you call `writeContractAsync`, wagmi asks the WalletConnect provider to send an `eth_sendTransaction` JSON-RPC request; that request is serialized, encrypted, and **published to the relay**, which pushes it to Rainbow. That part works — which is exactly why the request \"is waiting inside\" when the user switches manually.\n\nWhat is missing is **foregrounding the wallet app**. WC v2 sessions carry `peer.metadata.redirect` (a `native` scheme like `rainbow://` and/or a `universal` https link) precisely so the SDK can deep-link back to the wallet on each request. RainbowKit does attempt this. The reason it silently fails:\n\n- Mobile OSes (iOS especially) only allow a page to navigate to another app's scheme **inside a live user-activation (tap) context**.\n- `writeContractAsync` is **async**: it encodes args, estimates gas, and only then dispatches the RPC request over the relay. All of that happens *after* one or more `await`s.\n- By the time the redirect would fire, the user-activation from the \"Stake\" tap has already been **consumed / expired**, so the OS refuses the app switch.\n\nNet result: request delivered to Rainbow over the relay ✅, wallet never brought to the foreground ❌ → \"tapping Stake does nothing, but the request is there if I open Rainbow myself.\"\n\n## 2. Why the patch made it worse\n\n```js\nwindow.location.href = \"rainbow://\"   // fires immediately on tap\nawait writeContractAsync(...)          // request not sent yet\n```\n\nTwo problems, both fatal:\n\n1. **Ordering / race.** The deep link fires *before* `writeContractAsync` has produced and published the `eth_sendTransaction` to the relay. Rainbow foregrounds to a home screen with **no pending request** — there is genuinely nothing to sign yet.\n2. **Backgrounding the dApp kills the send.** Navigating away suspends/throttles the browser tab's JS. The async work in `writeContractAsync` (gas estimation, relay publish) may stall or never complete, so the request often never even reaches the relay. Bare `rainbow://` also has no request path — it just opens the app home.\n\nSo the patch converted \"opens late/never, but request exists\" into \"opens instantly, request never exists.\"\n\n## 3. The correct pattern\n\n**Fire the request first, then deep-link after a short delay — do not await before linking.**\n\n```js\nasync function onStake() {\n  if (!shouldDeepLink()) {            // see skip rules below\n    return writeContractAsync(txArgs);\n  }\n\n  const scheme = await getWalletScheme(); // from session metadata, not hardcoded\n\n  // 1. kick off the write — DON'T await it here\n  const txPromise = writeContractAsync(txArgs);\n\n  // 2. give WalletConnect time to publish the request to the relay,\n  //    then foreground the wallet\n  setTimeout(() => {\n    if (scheme) window.location.href = scheme;\n  }, 300);\n\n  return txPromise;\n}\n```\n\n**Ordering.** Start `writeContractAsync` *before* the deep link so the `eth_sendTransaction` is in flight to the relay. Do **not** `await` it before linking — the promise only resolves after the user signs, which is far too late to switch apps.\n\n**The delay and why its length matters.** The `setTimeout` must be:\n- **long enough** for the WC client to encode and publish the request over the relay (a network hop to the relay server — tens to low-hundreds of ms), so the request is already present/arriving when Rainbow comes forward;\n- **short enough** to still fire the app-switch while the tap's user activation is usable and before the browser fully suspends the tab.\n\n`~200–300 ms` is the practical sweet spot. `0` (the patch) opens before the request exists; multi-second delays lose the gesture and feel broken.\n\n**Which scheme to open.** `connector.id` is always the generic `\"walletConnect\"` — it tells you nothing about *which* wallet. Read the actual wallet from the **session peer metadata** instead of hardcoding `rainbow://`:\n\n```js\nasync function getWalletScheme() {\n  const provider = await connector.getProvider();\n  const redirect = provider?.session?.peer?.metadata?.redirect;\n  // prefer universal (https) link — works whether or not the app is installed\n  // and avoids the \"cannot open page\" error a bad custom scheme throws\n  return redirect?.universal || redirect?.native || null;\n}\n```\n\nUse `redirect.universal` first, fall back to `redirect.native`. This makes it work for Rainbow, MetaMask mobile, Trust, etc. without a hardcoded map. If there is no `redirect`, don't guess a scheme — skip.\n\n**When to skip the deep link entirely:**\n- **Not WalletConnect.** Injected / browser-extension connectors (`connector.id !== \"walletConnect\"`, e.g. MetaMask extension, Coinbase Wallet extension) — the wallet is in-process; deep-linking would break the flow.\n- **Desktop.** No wallet app to foreground; the QR/modal handles it. Gate on mobile UA / touch.\n- **In-app browser.** The dApp is already running inside the wallet's own dApp browser (provider is injected, `isInAppBrowser`-style). The request surfaces automatically; a scheme switch is wrong/redundant.\n- **No redirect metadata available.** Unknown wallet with no `session.peer.metadata.redirect` — skip rather than guess.\n- **Smart-wallet / popup flows** (e.g. Coinbase Smart Wallet) that use their own popup/redirect mechanism.\n\n**Better still:** most of this is what RainbowKit's own request-time redirect already tries to do. Before adding manual deep-link code, upgrade RainbowKit/`@walletconnect` — the reliable long-term fix is keeping the SDK's built-in redirect working rather than racing it by hand. If you must patch manually, use the ordering + metadata-driven scheme + skip rules above.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5544,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5544},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d6628738-ad41-4cec-873c-3befe5494f62","uuid":"11de1712-7300-48d5-8df0-589381f1f3a9","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:10:02.689Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6NKywCG8EBx5E8YULY"}

Summary of the three parts:\n\n**1. Why nothing auto-opened before the patch.** On mobile the dApp (browser tab) and Rainbow (separate app) share nothing — the WC v2 session runs over the relay websocket. `writeContractAsync` *does* publish the `eth_sendTransaction` to the relay (that's why the request \"is waiting\" if you switch manually). What fails is foregrounding the wallet: RainbowKit tries to deep-link using `session.peer.metadata.redirect`, but because `writeContractAsync` is async (encode → gas-estimate → publish, all after `await`s), the tap's **user-activation** is already consumed by the time the redirect fires, so iOS silently blocks the app switch.\n\n**2. Why the patch made it worse.** `window.location.href = \"rainbow://\"` fires *before* the request is published — Rainbow opens to its home screen with nothing pending. Worse, navigating away backgrounds the tab, throttling the JS so the relay publish often never completes. It turned \"opens late, request exists\" into \"opens instantly, request never exists.\"\n\n**3. Summary of the three parts:\n\n**1. Why nothing auto-opened before the patch.** On mobile the dApp (browser tab) and Rainbow (separate app) share nothing — the WC v2 session runs over the relay websocket. `writeContractAsync` *does* publish the `eth_sendTransaction` to the relay (that's why the request \"is waiting\" if you switch manually). What fails is foregrounding the wallet: RainbowKit tries to deep-link using `session.peer.metadata.redirect`, but because `writeContractAsync` is async (encode → gas-estimate → publish, all after `await`s), the tap's **user-activation** is already consumed by the time the redirect fires, so iOS silently blocks the app switch.\n\n**2. Why the patch made it worse.** `window.location.href = \"rainbow://\"` fires *before* the request is published — Rainbow opens to its home screen with nothing pending. Worse, navigating away backgrounds the tab, throttling the JS so the relay publish often never completes. It turned \"opens late, request exists\" into \"opens instantly, request never exists.\"\n\n**3. Correct pattern.**\n- **Order:** start `writeContractAsync` first (don't await it), *then* deep-link.\n- **Delay:** `setTimeout(~200–300ms)` — long enough for the WC client to publish the request to the relay, short enough to keep the user-gesture valid and beat tab suspension. `0` opens too early; seconds lose the gesture.\n- **Scheme:** `connector.id` is always `\"walletConnect\"` and useless for this — read `provider.session.peer.metadata.redirect`, preferring `.universal` (https) over `.native` (custom scheme). No hardcoded `rainbow://`.\n- **Skip when:** connector isn't WalletConnect (injected/extension), desktop, running inside a wallet in-app browser, no `redirect` metadata, or smart-wallet/popup flows.\n- **Note:** the durable fix is upgrading RainbowKit/`@walletconnect` so its built-in request-time redirect works, rather than racing it manually.","ttft_ms":45609,"ttft_stream_ms":1538,"time_to_request_ms":20,"type":"result","duration_ms":89246,"uuid":"d18f4608-4f4c-474e-aec9-8d37847dd6c1"}
